extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in culture, women's media, comedy; aspiring satire writers and editors
extracted.subtask_description: Creating satire and parody that targets media directed at women (magazines, blogs, lifestyle outlets), often in an Onion-style news-parody/online-comedy format. Emphasis on tone, headline craft, and topical choices that expose contradictions and pressures in women's media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirize media directed toward women (and the industry itself)
rubrics_metrics.description: “more specifically satirize media directed toward women, and the industry itself.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target the conventions, tone, and business practices of outlets aimed at women (magazines, blogs, lifestyle companies). Examples cited: Cosmopolitan, Shape, Jezebel, xoJane, 'inspirational' blogosphere, Kinfolk-inspired media, the 'hip' New York media company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary goal: be funny
rubrics_metrics.description: “Well, the one main goal of the site is to be funny. We want to write things that make people laugh and help them get through their day jobs.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor is the top criterion; satire should prioritize comedic impact while delivering critique. Make pieces that elicit laughter and provide entertainment value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring true and feel fresh and original
rubrics_metrics.description: “We want things to always ring true and to feel fresh and original.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid stale, recycled jokes. Satire should capture recognizable truths about the target while presenting them in novel ways so readers recognize the target and are surprised by the treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move beyond a strict news-parody format
rubrics_metrics.description: “We do want to move beyond a strict news format—taking on the women’s ‘inspirational’ blogosphere, the Kinfolk-inspired media, and the very idea of the 'hip' New York media company itself.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t limit satire to mock news articles; parody blogs, listicles, how-tos, advertorials, and lifestyle-features as needed to hit different targets and tones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mimic format and tone of target publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Site is “designed to look like any other ‘women's’ publication” (a clear play on magazines like Cosmopolitan and Shape and feminist websites like Jezebel and xoJane).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt layout, headline style, voice, and rhetorical conventions of the target so the parody reads as an authentic incarnation of that media, enhancing satirical contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose contradictory messaging in women's media
rubrics_metrics.description: “There’s just a whole lot of other silly stuff out there... I’m fascinated by the well-meaning, but completely contradictory messages that women are 'beautiful no matter what,' but that 'beauty lies on the inside.' We’re being fed completely different messages in the same tone...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight and amplify internal contradictions in messaging (e.g., empowerment rhetoric coexisting with prescriptive beauty advice) to reveal absurdity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirize pressure to meet arbitrary 'real woman' checkboxes
rubrics_metrics.description: “One of the overriding themes we’re parodying is the pressure women’s media puts on women and girls to be a certain type of person or check a certain number of boxes to be a ‘real’ woman.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target standards, checklists, and gatekeeping language that define womanhood; show how publications demand conformity through lists, quizzes, and 'must-do' items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique sensationalist, traffic-chasing headline culture
rubrics_metrics.description: “We know there’s pressure for the people who work at these publications and blogs to come up with sensational headlines to generate traffic and we’re really amused by the lengths they’ll go to in order to do that.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hyperbolic or clickbait headlines to lampoon the lengths outlets go to for clicks; headlines themselves can be the primary satirical device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover topics underrepresented in mainstream comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: “Hopefully, we’re covering topics that women don’t get to see represented elsewhere in comedy.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose subject matter and perspectives that are rarely addressed in male-dominated comedy spaces, centering women’s experiences, anxieties, and institutional pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use biting, 'goes-there' humor to reveal sad/necessary truths
rubrics_metrics.description: Reductress is described as “not only biting, ‘goes-there’ hilarious, it’s a fantastic, sad, and much-needed look at the way the media talks down to women...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to use dark or uncomfortable jokes to expose real harms and social dynamics; balance edge with clear critical intent so satire punches up and informs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ satirical devices: juxtaposition, minimization, exaggeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample headlines illustrate technique: “Creator of 'Rape in America' Documentary Talks About Hair Care,” “A Homemaker’s Guide to Maybe Thinking About Wanting to Have Sex?,” “Bologna for Her.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques shown include juxtaposing serious topics with trivial concerns, minimizing or misframing harms to reveal absurdity, and exaggerating marketing/gossip to highlight distortions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize relevance to actual people over demographic-targeted filler
rubrics_metrics.description: “There is so much content out there that is catered to women (the demographic) that is of questionable relevance to women (the actual human beings). The more we are engulfed in it, the harder it is to see just how absurd it is.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create satire that speaks to lived experiences and meaningful critiques rather than pandering to a demographic profile; aim for specificity that resonates with real readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt an obsessive writing and editing process
rubrics_metrics.description: Beth Newell references loving “their obsessive writing process” at The Onion News Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat satire as craft: iterate, workshop, and edit headlines and body copy carefully (similar to The Onion's process) to sharpen jokes and ensure targets are clear.
